title: Zoroaster
author: Unknown
description: Life and Teachings of Zoroaster, the Great Persian by Loren Harper Whitney of the Chicago Bar (Chicago: de Laurence, Scott & Co., 1905), a study of the ancient Iranian prophet Zarathustra and the religion he founded. Part One recounts the traditions of Zoroaster's life, his call and revelations from Ahura Mazda, his struggle against the priests and the conversion of King Vishtaspa, and surveys the Avesta and the Gathas. The author then sets out Zoroastrian teaching on the one wise Lord, the conflict between the good spirit and the evil Angra Mainyu, the moral triad of good thoughts, good words and good deeds, the Amesha Spentas, judgement at the Chinvat Bridge, resurrection and the final renovation of the world. Part Two argues that much of Jewish and Christian belief came 'by way of Persia'. It reflects the comparative-religion enthusiasm of its era.
